text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated p99/p95 latency on inference path — streaming stalls starting ~09:02 UTC. Paging oncall. Severity: P1.

maya_oncall: on it. seeing p95 ~ 320ms -> 750ms, p99 spikes to 2.4s. streaming tail stalls + partial reconnects.

maya_oncall: initial alert came from streaming-monitor: 40% of streams reported 10s+ stall windows. Affected routes: /v1/generate (stream), /v1/chat/stream.

oliver_csm: customers reporting sessions drop and a couple saying UI shows "waiting for response..." for >30s. No full data loss but UX broken for some PLG customers.

liam_dbops: looking at control-plane logs. config-fetch upstream to config-store (postgres) showing repeated 5xx timeouts and auth token fetch 502s. DB connection count jumped ~3x at 09:00 UTC.

liam_dbops: also seeing rate-limit counters on token-service -> token-store (429s) from control-plane sidecars. lots of backpressure.

tj: stack traces point to featureflag eval path adding a synchronous call per request. If ff store is slow, it blocks request path -> streaming stalls.

sara_platform: rolling out request flow: model routing checks -> feature flag check -> config fetch -> policy evaluation -> serve. That synchronous ff/config chain explains tail.

maya_oncall: immediate mitigation idea: flip FF to cached mode or bypass per-request eval for streaming requests, and increase config TTL. Can someone run the admin toggle?

jen_k8s: I can apply a canary change to disable ff eval in the control-plane Deployment. quick command:```bash
kubectl -n control-plane set env deploy/control-plane FEATUREFLAGS_PER_REQUEST=false
```

jen_k8s: but that will be a deployment env update and triggers restart. prefer doing a runtime toggle via admin API if available.

liam_dbops: DB: long running queries on config_store:```
SELECT * FROM feature_flag_revocations WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '5 minutes';
```seeing locking on index feature_flag_revocations_pkey. I can scale read replicas and bump pool.

tj: admin API to set cache TTL:```
POST /admin/featureflags/cache
{ "ttl_seconds": 300 }
```That would stop sync fetches for 5 minutes.

maya_oncall: who can call that admin API? jen_k8s? deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: Automated admin calls require service token. @jen_k8s has the token, @maya_oncall has emergency key.

jen_k8s: executing now. hitting admin endpoint... response 200. Cache TTL set to 300s.

incident-bot: ACTION_CREATED: increase-config-cache-ttl by jen_k8s (runbook-step-2).

maya_oncall: also asking to temporarily relax token-store rate limits between control-plane and token-store for 15m. liam, can you coordinate DB-side throttle window?

liam_dbops: yes. bumping rate-limit window and increasing conn pool:```
-- psql
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 120; -- apply via cloud sql
-- then roll pooler config
```Applying now.

liam_dbops: scaled read replicas + restarted pgbouncer. monitoring.

tj: after TTL toggle + DB bump: p95 down to ~280ms, p99 down to ~1.1s. streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.

maya_oncall: partial success. still seeing tail spikes on a subset of tenants (dedicated customers). Likely hitting local sidecar auth path or regional token-store intermittency.

oliver_csm: reaching out to impacted customers with an update. telling them we have mitigations in place and ETA for full resolution ~30–60m.

jen_k8s: next mitigation: enable fallback model routing to lighter-weight model variant to reduce end-to-end compute latency for affected tenants. Can be toggled per-tenant.

tj: note: fallback will reduce quality slightly but improves tail latency. propose enabling for 10% of affected tenants as canary.

maya_oncall: proceed with canary. jen, can you push per-tenant routing override?

jen_k8s: doing override for tenant group "plg-alpha" -> routing.override=true. command:```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/api/tenants/plg-alpha/overrides -d '{"model":"gptx-small","enabled":true}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for routing override.

tj: metrics: for affected streams where override applied, p99 ~ 650ms. good improvement. overall p99 for system now ~900ms.

liam_dbops: token-store logs show fewer 429s since rate-limit bump. DB replication lag minimal.

maya_oncall: customer impact classification: partial degradation for streaming features (~30% of sessions affected earlier), now reduced to ~8% with mitigations. No data loss. Severity remains P1 until fully stable.

oliver_csm: sending second customer update: summary of what we changed (cache TTL, rate-limit bump, read-replica scale, routing fallback canary).

maya_oncall: next steps: 1) monitor 15m for stability 2) if stable, revert aggressive overrides and roll proper config-cache/ff-service fix 3) schedule postmortem with root cause analysis.

tj: root cause hypothesis: synchronous feature-flag/config fetch in control-plane combined with token-store auth rate-limiting under a traffic surge -> cascading tail latency for streaming. Need a durable fix: async ff evaluation, local caching, pre-warm tokens.

jen_k8s: creating infra task to add circuit-breaker and fallback path in control-plane. also ticket to move heavy ff evals off hot path.

liam_dbops: I'll follow up with DB tuning doc and create runbook item to scale read replicas automatically on auth spikes.

maya_oncall: handing off to @tj for the next hour. I'm putting the channel into watch-only and will join in 30 if needed.

tj: übernehmen. keeping watch. please DM if anything urgent.

incident-bot: ONCALL_HANDOFF: from maya_oncall -> tj at 09:12 UTC.

maya_oncall: final note: collect logs for 09:00–09:10 UTC for affected tenant IDs and upload to /incident-archive/1769504321. include control-plane logs, token-store, pgbouncer, and streaming-monitor traces.

oliver_csm: I logged customer comms in zendesk and added incident update reference id 1769504321.

tj: monitoring looks stable at 09:20 UTC. keeping P1 active until 1hr stable.

jen_k8s: created PR for nonblocking ff cache + circuit-breaker: https://git.internal/r/redwood/control-plane/pulls/4321

liam_dbops: DB metrics look healthy. closing immediate DB scaling actions but keeping replica warm.

maya_oncall: thanks team. we'll do a postmortem once we collect more traces. tagging for follow-ups: @sara_platform (observability), @tj (follow-up on canary), @liam_dbops (db tuning), @jen_k8s (infra fixes), @oliver_csm (customer comms). :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: mitigations applied, partial recovery observed. next update or final resolution will be posted to this thread.
